bibl.title: The Hymn of Mesomedes on Antinous (Inscription of Courion, Mitford No. 104).
bibl.seg: Egert Pöhlmann, The Hymn of Mesomedes on Antinous (Inscription of Courion, Mitford No. 104).
Greek and Roman Musical Studies 7 (2019) pp. 128-139, figg.
bibl.note: In his publication of the inscriptions of Courion (10 km west of Limassol) Mitford recognized clearly that the Antinous in Courion no. 104 must be the paidika of the Emperor Hadrian, and that the hymn in the inscription must be an encomium to Antinous, who drowned in the waters of the Nile in 130 AD. By comparing the metrics and the style of the encomium with the preserved poetry of Mesomedes, argues that the hymn on Antinous is the encomium attested by the Suda for Mesomedes.
